feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 7 (16 mm, ±0.06 m span, 0.6 kg, y = 0.02 m, kp 2.2, kd 0.5) gave 14 of 20 oval completions and slalom line_loss_events of 0.3. Iteration 8 (same, 12 mm) gave 0 oval completions and slalom line loss of 0.25, so the footprint must stay at 16 mm and the span is the remaining lever. I have kept gains and body, mass, track and wheels fixed, so the span is the only change. Next race: if slalom line_loss_events fall below about 0.25 while oval completions stay at about 14 of 20 or better, keep ±0.07 m and move the sharp-bend effort to turn authority (wheel_track). If oval completions fall while line loss falls, the weights are too large for the wider span, so keep the geometry and let the Integrator rescale. If line loss does not fall, the outer edge is not the limit, and the next test is wheel_track 0.11 m.
requested_changes: If slalom line_loss_events stay at or above about 0.25 with the ±0.07 m span and 16 mm sensors (iteration 7 at ±0.06 m gave 0.3): keep sensor_size 0.016 m, and try wheel_track 0.11 m, because the s-bend and slalom have never produced progress above 0.3 (iteration 7 s-bend 0.27, slalom 0.12).

If oval completions fall below about 12 of 20 with the wider span (iteration 7 gave 14 of 20 at ±0.06 m): return sensor_size to 0.016 m and keep the iteration 7 span at ±0.06 m. Iteration 8 showed 12 mm drops completions to 0, so do not reduce the footprint again.

If line loss falls but the s-bend and slalom still end off track with no progress above 0.5: keep ±0.07 m and try mass 0.7 kg with body_length 0.12 m, because iteration 5 (0.8 kg, 0.16 m body) had zero slalom line loss, and the heavier robot may hold the line through the sharp bends.
